title: lore check charges a worst-case query section that no task renders, so its capacity number is not the pack it certifies
description:
Since LCLI-662 (DEC-98 B) the agent-profile capacity measurement adds a query-section reserve to the declared set, so a budget that satisfies the check cannot start dropping declared evidence on a real task. The reserve is `worstCaseQuerySectionTokens(graph)`: a `Math.max` over five synthetic section shapes built from the bundle and independent of any task. Task-independence is the property the CHECK needs — its verdict has to be the same on every task, which is what separates it from task-ranked omission — so reserving a worst case there is deliberate.

What it is not is the pack. `compilePack` renders ONE section, whose shape depends on the task, and the reserve is by construction the shape that maximises across all of them, so a real pack can spend strictly less. The check therefore reports a number the pack it is certifying never spends, and once DEC-11's flip lands (LCLI-646) that number FAILS a profile on a measurement no task produces.

Measured on this repository's own four profiles: the reserve is 360 tokens on every one of them, identical because the reserve depends only on the bundle and not on the profile.

TWO FIXES, and which one is a design call rather than this task's: (i) check measures what compile renders; or (ii) the finding names the difference, stating that the reserve is a worst case that a task-dependent pack may not spend. Either way the report must stop presenting the reserve as the pack's own figure.

Filed per opum-doc's ruling DEC-194 (6), recorded at opum-ai/opum-doc#1031. The acceptance criterion that matters most is proving it on opum-ai/opum-cli's `review` profile read from `origin/main` (`.lore/agents/review.toml`, `max_tokens = 11880`), because that is a real consumer whose budget the reserve can fail.

acceptanceCriteria.text: lore check no longer presents a worst-case reserve as the pack own number: either the figure it reports is one compileAgentContext also renders, or the finding names the reserve as a worst case that a task-dependent pack may not spend.

Proved on opum-ai/opum-cli review profile, read from origin/main at .lore/agents/review.toml (max_tokens = 11880, 4 whole-document pins, sources = [index]): the reserve lore check charges there and the query section that same profile renders for a real task are reported together, both figures named in the evidence.

The gap is QUANTIFIED rather than asserted: the token difference between the reserved worst case and the rendered section is stated, and which of the five reserve shapes produces the maximum is identified.

Both arms: a profile whose verdict differs between the reserve and the render (over by the reserve, within budget by the rendered section), or, if no real profile differs anywhere, the measured margin that shows why, named as a margin rather than reported as agreement.

A pack that a real task CAN render over budget is still caught, and the check verdict for one profile stays the same on every task: LCLI-662 guarantee and the check task-independence are each pinned by a test that goes red if that direction is dropped.
